column1: Applies to every domain event; EV-26 and EV-27 are exempt from the Transactions rule. EV-29 and EV-30 are not domain events.

column2: Events for one case are processed in the order they were written, by a sequence per case in the outbox
At least once; consumers are idempotent
Each event carries an event ID and an idempotency key; a repeat is ignored and counted (R-UNI-40)

The event is written in the same transaction as the change; no event without the change and no change without the event. EV-26 and EV-27 are exempt: they are raised from the ACE batch record, not from a Workbench change
References and codes; no personal data
An event carries its schema version; consumers accept the current and previous version
A consumer failure retries; after the limit the event goes to the exception queue with its owner
A Temporal signal goes to one workflow ID; it is not a broadcast, not a domain event and not written to the outbox
The outbox stays for outbound work in Epics 1 and 2; from Epic 3 the multi-step outbound chain on rwb-integration writes through the outbox before the external call
Temporal history is the workflow's own record; it is not an event bus and no consumer subscribes to it
